title: Vee's first storefront
question: Luxury rooted in nature: rich, comforting, and calming. Choose the storefront composition to build.

options.label: The forest sanctuary
options.lineage: A botanical cosmetic case opening onto pale stone terraces
options.thesis: A deep forest-green shell opens into a light stone collection, like a quiet garden sanctuary.
options.viewport: Vee sits above a still life of cosmetics, leaves, and stone; a light inset holds the collection action.
options.risk: The natural imagery expresses a feeling; it must never imply unverified natural ingredients.

raised.raise: Bag counts and selected shades keep stable positions across state changes.
Every selection, disabled control, and pressed state has an unmistakable visual signal.
One coordinated opening gesture replaces scattered decorative animations.
The collection has confident product density rather than endless oversized cards.
The Vee wordmark owns a decisive scale while all shopping labels remain readable.
The opening has one immersive botanical setting, while collection surfaces stay quiet.

options.label: The botanical atelier
options.thesis: A sunlit botanical studio presents cosmetics beside sculptural leaves and warm stone.
options.viewport: A spacious botanical still life shares the screen with an elegant headline and direct collection link.
options.risk: A familiar luxury campaign composition; the calm depends on excellent photography.

options.label: The amber light hall
options.thesis: Vee's collection occupies a vast amber-lit hall, with silhouettes and reflected selection states.
options.viewport: A luminous horizontal hall frames the product silhouette and a low, clear collection action.
options.case: The amber installation carries richness but loses the requested botanical comfort and cosmetic color clarity.
options.risk: Product detail screens must restore accurate product colors.
options.kept: One immersive environmental scene rather than competing decorations.

options.label: Seven-segment display
options.thesis: A fixed luminous mask organizes shade numbers and shopping counts.
options.viewport: Large fixed shade digits organize the product selection.
options.risk: Instrument controls obscure cosmetic names and read as electronics.
options.case: Loses both customer identification and product clarity for a first cosmetics storefront.
options.kept: Stable positions for shopping counts and shade states.

options.label: One-bit desktop
options.thesis: Products open in crisp monochrome windows on a single desktop plane.
options.viewport: A tiled cosmetic catalog opens into overlapping detail windows.
options.risk: One-bit product imagery cannot accurately communicate cosmetic colors.
options.case: Loses luxury identification and cosmetic shade clarity.
options.kept: Explicit selected, disabled, and pressed states.

options.label: Rubber-hose cel
options.thesis: Rounded cosmetic scenes arrive through an animated iris.
options.viewport: An oval product scene opens with rubbery shopping controls.
options.risk: Gag-driven movement distracts from evaluating products.
options.case: Loses luxury identification and a direct, legible shopping path.

options.label: Posada broadside
options.thesis: The cosmetic collection becomes a dense printed sheet under one engraved image band.
options.viewport: A shouting product headline leads into two tightly set collection columns.
options.risk: Cheap-paper printing and skeletal imagery conflict with the current luxury brief.
options.case: Loses customer identification and makes product comparison harder.
options.kept: Confident density for the collection layout.

options.label: Alphabet storm
options.thesis: Cosmetic category words gather and dissolve into a typographic landscape.
options.viewport: A large cosmetic category word transforms above the collection action.
options.risk: Word transformation demonstrates language rather than the cosmetics.
options.case: Loses customer identification and concrete product clarity.
options.kept: Decisive typographic scale with readable shopping labels.

canonCard.label: Classic luxury storefront
canonCard.thesis: A familiar luxury storefront with botanical photography, soft stone surfaces, and direct shopping.
canonCard.viewport: A familiar navigation bar, campaign image, shopping action, and featured product row.
canonCard.risk: Easy to understand, with less distinctive brand recognition.
